newsitem.title: USA: Caterpillar sees 1997 profit near '96 level.
newsitem.headline: Caterpillar sees 1997 profit near '96 level.

text.p: Caterpillar Inc said Tuesday it expected profit for 1997 to be near the 1996 level, while earnings per share will continue to benefit from the share repurchase program begun in June 1995.
Earlier Tuesday, the heavy equipment maker reported net income of $1.36 billion, or $7.07 a share, for 1996, up from $1.14 billion, or $5.72 a share a year ago.
The company also said it expected revenues from ongoing operations to slightly surpass the $16.52 billion reported for 1996.
Higher industry demand in developing regions should offset slightly lower industry demand in the United States and Japan, Caterpillar said.

Sales improvement should come from an increase in market share and limited price increases, Cateprillar said. The acquisition of engine maker MaK Motoren GmbH should also boost sales, Caterpillar said.

Caterpillar reported margins as a percent of sales of 25.2 percent in 1996, compared to 22.3 percent in 1995, due to higher prices and the effect of the stronger dollar against the yen and European currencies.
Lower material costs and improvements in the manufacturing process also helped Caterpillar.
Margins in the fourth quarter were 25.8 percent, compared to 22.9 percent a year ago, Caterpillar said.
Total capital expenditures in 1996 were $642 million and are expected to increase 10 to 15 percent in 1997, Caterpillar said.

"In 1997, we plan to increase spending for capital assets, research and product development to enhance our prospects for long-term growth and profitability," Caterpillar chairman and chief executive Donald Fites said in a news release. "In addition, we intend to increase our investments for new business opportunities around the globe."
Major initiatives include electric power generation, agricultural products, mining systems, compact machines and strengthening the company's product support system, Caterpillar said.
Research and development expenditures are expected to rise 20 percent from the $410 million spent in 1996, Caterpillar said.

The company said it expects world economic growth excludign the Commonwealth of independent States, should be similar to 1996. Economic recovery is expected in the former Soviet Union states, Cateprillar said.
Caterpillar expects U.S. gross domestic product growth of two percent in 1997, down from about 2.5 percent in 1996
